setup: Two solids are similar, with every length in the larger \([[factor]]\) times the corresponding length in the smaller.

steps.say: The length ratio is applied once per dimension, so surface area -- which has two dimensions -- scales by \([[area_ratio]]\).
Volume has three dimensions, so it scales by the cube of the length ratio: \([[factor]]^3 = [[volume_ratio]]\). That is why a model at a small scale holds far less than it looks like it should.

answer: So the larger solid's volume is \([[volume_ratio]]\) times the smaller's.
